comparisons.peer_summary: Transfers into level 3 in 2023 involved equity and corporate debt securities from level 2 due to reduced price transparency and significant unobservable yield inputs, while transfers out occurred due to increased price transparency and less significant unobservable inputs.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS disclose Level 3 transfers occurring during the period ended December 31, 2023 (C in the 12 months ended 12/31/23, GS in 2023). Both companies attribute transfers into Level 3 to reduced price transparency or observability and the significance of unobservable inputs. However, the instruments differ: C reports transfers primarily involving Long-term debt (structured and interest rate/equity derivative inputs), whereas GS reports transfers involving equity and corporate debt securities driven by reduced market transactions and yield inputs.

sentences.text: During the 12 months ended December 31, 2023, transfers of Long-term debt were $4.9 billion from Level 2 to Level 3.

Of the $4.9 billion transfer, approximately $4.2 billion related to interest rate option volatility inputs becoming unobservable and/or significant relative to their overall valuation, and $0.6 billion related to equity and credit derivative inputs (in addition to other volatility inputs, e.g., interest rate volatility inputs) becoming unobservable and/or significant to their overall valuation.

Transfers into level 3 investments during 2023 primarily reflected transfers of certain equity securities and corporate debt securities from level 2 (in each case, principally due to reduced price transparency as a result of a lack of market evidence, including fewer market transactions in these instruments, and certain unobservable yield inputs becoming significant to the valuation of these instruments).

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, significant fair value transfers occurred between Level 2 and Level 3, including $1.0 billion of debt/equity and derivative instruments into Level 3 due to decreased observability, and $880 million of debt/equity and $1.4-2.0 billion of equity derivatives out of Level 3 due to increased observability.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose Level 3 transfers driven by changes in observability and the significance of unobservable inputs. A key difference is the time period: C reports transfers for the 12 months ended December 31, 2023, while JPM reports transfers for the year ended December 31, 2024. Both note long-term debt transfers: C transferred $4.9B of long-term debt into Level 3 due to unobservable volatility inputs, while JPM transferred $863M of long-term debt out of Level 3 into Level 2 due to increased observability.

sentences.text: During the 12 months ended December 31, 2023, transfers of Long-term debt were $4.9 billion from Level 2 to Level 3.

Of the $4.9 billion transfer, approximately $4.2 billion related to interest rate option volatility inputs becoming unobservable and/or significant relative to their overall valuation, and $0.6 billion related to equity and credit derivative inputs (in addition to other volatility inputs, e.g., interest rate volatility inputs) becoming unobservable and/or significant to their overall valuation.
This has primarily resulted in $10.2 billion of certain structured long-term debt products being transferred from Level 3 to Level 2 during the 12 months ended December 31, 2023.
• $863 million of long-term debt as a result of an increase in observability and a decrease in the significance of unobservable inputs.
